name: Recital 3
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on applying a generalised scheme of tariff preferences and repealing Regulation (EU) No 978/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text: (3) The Union's common commercial policy, including the scheme of generalised tariff preferences, should primarily promote international trade and economic development in partner countries while safeguarding the competitiveness of Union industry. It shall comply with World Trade Organisation (WTO) requirements, in particular with the Decision on Differential and More Favourable Treatment, Reciprocity and Fuller Participation of Developing Countries (the ‘Enabling Clause’), adopted under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in 1979, under which WTO Members may accord differential and more favourable treatment to developing countries. The scheme should not be turned into an instrument for pursuing broader external, climate or social policy aims going beyond the Union’s explicit trade competences under the Treaties.
